status: SOURCE ELIGIBILITY PASS FOR BOUNDED FACE STUDY; COMPLETED SILHOUETTE ACCEPTANCE HELD
scope: Independent visual reading of cached primary photographs and the P5 proposal only. No candidate geometry/render inspected; no modelling, GPU, root edit, publication or dimensional authentication performed.

primaryReferences.title: Library of Congress, Detroit Publishing photograph item
ASCE volume 69, plate LXXXIV Fig.2, cached scan context

features.feature: Broad stringer cheeks and continuous horizontal landing-side band
features.photoSupport: Clearly visible in both LOC crops, particularly the central lower two-flight stairs. Large unbroken visible side faces are supported.
features.candidateAcceptance: Eligible as a bounded appearance study. Require continuous visible faces and restrained seams in a comparable oblique view.
features.notEstablished: Photographs do not prove an 8 mm cover sheet, hollow closed section, host I-section dimensions or a particular fabrication method.

features.photoSupport: Both LOC crops show the sloping lower edge easing into the horizontal landing/fascia profile with smooth curvature.
features.candidateAcceptance: A straight-panel-only result cannot establish a completed historical stair silhouette. Compare the candidate lower outline and landing haunches explicitly; treat missing curves as a remaining geometry stage.
features.notEstablished: Exact radius, curve construction, section thickness and uniformity across all platforms are not recoverable from these perspective crops alone.

features.feature: Handrail direction changes and returned ends
features.photoSupport: Visible handrail changes of direction and terminal/landing returns are smooth curved forms; the rail relates to the shaped newel tops.
features.candidateAcceptance: Inspect actual candidate rail transitions separately from flat skins. Retaining old rails preserves existing contacts but does not certify their photographic fidelity.
features.notEstablished: Exact rail diameter, bend radius, connection fabrication and every return arrangement are unmeasured.

features.photoSupport: Ball finials, shaped shoulders/shafts and visible plinth/collar or shoe forms occur in the source stairs.
features.candidateAcceptance: Preserve structural anchors in the bounded study. Any later visible profile revision requires a dedicated silhouette trace and source-classification note.
features.notEstablished: The photographs do not establish the buried bearing-pad elevation or justify a 207.5 mm raise, nor do they provide exact base profiles for all instances.

features.feature: Gallery fascia and distinct deck levels
features.photoSupport: Exposed horizontal edge bands and open views below/beside the decks are visible. The prominent rounded upper-concourse fascia and lower Exit-gallery edge are different visible contexts.
features.candidateAcceptance: Identify the actual lower-gallery edge before matching profiles. Preserve open rail/track views. Use a bounded face as a study, not as proof of the entire historical edge section.
features.notEstablished: Do not transfer the upper-concourse moulded-looking edge profile to the lower gallery without registered evidence. Skin seams, 430 mm height and exact section remain authored assumptions.

features.photoSupport: Vertical divisions, diagonal motifs and circular junction details are visible.
features.candidateAcceptance: Existing guards may remain as a protected control in this study; historical completion requires a separate comparison of panel rhythm and connections.
features.notEstablished: The photographs do not prove the candidate bar counts, diameters, every ornament profile or 1935 retention.

overallHolds: These crops do not identify P5; use a typical arrival-stair-family comparison, not an authenticated P5 matching-camera claim.
Opening-era photographic evidence does not establish complete 1935–1940 retention, colour or service inventory.
No sheet thickness, precise curve radius, paint colour, material alloy, full bearing area or structural capacity is authenticated by this visual review.
Physical contact/ownership/encoding tests are separate and are not replaced by photographic silhouette agreement.
recommendedReviewViews: Oblique side view of the complete two-flight arrival stair, including intermediate landing and both exposed side profiles.
Close view of the sloped-to-level lower stringer outline and the corresponding handrail/newel transitions.
Wider lower-gallery view identifying the lower Exit fascia separately from the upper-concourse edge.
promotionRecommendation: Review the bounded flat-face prototype as an intermediate appearance study. Do not label it a finished historic stair or repeat it as a completed profile until the curved transitions and correct deck-level silhouette have been assessed.
